extra.message: SQL injection: the student name supplied via POST /students/ (sqli/views.py:55-57, request.post()['name']) is interpolated into the SQL string with %-formatting ("INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name} at lines 42-43) and executed by cur.execute(q) at line 45 with no parameterization. An attacker can submit a name such as "x'); DROP TABLE students;--" to inject arbitrary SQL, allowing data exfiltration, modification or deletion of the entire database.

Cross-site scripting: Jinja2 is set up with autoescape=False for all templates. User-controlled data (student names, course titles/descriptions, review texts) is rendered in templates without the 'e' filter, so every template output of user data becomes an XSS sink (see sqli/templates/students.jinja2:16, courses.jinja2:17-18, course.jinja2:14-15,22,49, review.jinja2:32, evaluate.jinja2:25).

Stored XSS: the student name ({{ name }}) is rendered unescaped. Student names are attacker-controlled through the unauthenticated POST /students/ endpoint (sqli/views.py:54-57 -> Student.create) and Jinja autoescaping is disabled (sqli/app.py:35), so a name like "<script>alert(1)</script>" executes in every visitor's browser on the students listing page.

Stored XSS: course title ({{ course.title }}, line 17) and description ({{ course.description }}, line 18) are rendered unescaped. These fields are attacker-controlled through the POST /courses/ endpoint (sqli/views.py:86-90 -> Course.create) which has no authentication, and Jinja autoescaping is disabled (sqli/app.py:35), enabling persistent script injection rendered to all users.

Stored XSS: the course review text ({{ review.review_text }}) is rendered unescaped on the course detail page. Review text is attacker-controlled via the public POST /courses/{id}/review endpoint (sqli/views.py:119-130 -> Review.create) and autoescaping is disabled (sqli/app.py:35), so any anonymous user can persist a JavaScript payload that executes for every visitor. {{ course.title }} and {{ course.description }} on lines 14-15 and {{ student.name }} on line 49 are additional unescaped user-controlled sinks in this template.

XSS: the course title is rendered unescaped in "Write review to {{ course.title }}" (line 32) while line 10 of the same template correctly applies the '| e' escape filter. Course titles are attacker-controlled via POST /courses/ (sqli/views.py:86-90) and autoescaping is globally disabled (sqli/app.py:35), so a crafted title executes script in the review form page.

XSS: the student name is rendered unescaped in "Back to student {{ student.name }}" (line 25; line 9 of the same template uses '| e'). Student names are attacker-controlled via POST /students/ (sqli/views.py:54-57) and autoescaping is globally disabled (sqli/app.py:35), so a crafted student name executes script when the evaluation error page is rendered.

Missing authentication for a critical function: the POST branch of the students handler creates new students (Student.create) without any authentication check. The UI only shows the add-student form to logged-in users (sqli/templates/students.jinja2 '{% if auth_user %}'), but the handler enforces nothing, so anonymous users can create arbitrary students (and thereby inject SQL via sqli/dao/student.py:42-45 or stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Missing authorization: the POST branch of the courses handler creates new courses without any authentication or admin check, although the UI restricts the add-course form to admin users (sqli/templates/courses.jinja2 '{% if auth_user and auth_user.is_admin %}'). Any anonymous user can create courses (enabling stored XSS and data pollution).

Missing authorization: the evaluate handler (POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id}) records marks without any authentication or authorization check. The UI presents this action only to admin users (sqli/templates/course.jinja2 '{% if auth_user.is_admin %}'), but the handler enforces nothing, so any anonymous user can create arbitrary marks for any student/course.

Passwords are hashed and compared using unsalted MD5: check_password() compares pwd_hash to md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(). MD5 is cryptographically broken and far too fast for password hashing, allowing efficient brute-force and rainbow-table attacks against leaked hashes (migrations/001-fixtures.sql confirms hashes like md5('password')). A salted slow KDF (bcrypt/scrypt/argon2) should be used.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: CSRF protection is disabled: the csrf_middleware implemented in sqli/middlewares.py:26-38 is commented out of the application middleware stack ('# csrf_middleware,'), while templates still emit _csrf_token values. All state-changing POST endpoints (login, logout, student/course/review creation, evaluation) can be forged by a cross-site request from any page the victim visits.

The session cookie is created with httponly=False (RedisStorage(app['redis'], httponly=False)), exposing the session identifier to JavaScript; the 'secure' flag is also not set, so the cookie is transmitted over plain HTTP. Combined with the XSS vulnerabilities in the templates, this allows session token theft and session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Flag

extra.message: The web application is instantiated with debug=True, enabling debug behavior and verbose internal error details in the served application (run.py also sets logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)).

Information disclosure: the 50x error handler (sqli/middlewares.py:68-72, handle_50x) renders the raw exception attributes to the client via '
{{ error.__dict__ }}
', leaking internal error details (e.g. database/SQL errors, internal paths and state) to end users, which aids further attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded database credentials: the default application configuration (used by default at sqli/app.py:18, commandline.standard_argparse_options(ap, default_config='./config/dev.yaml')) contains the database superuser name 'postgres' and password 'postgres' in plaintext.

Hardcoded weak default credentials: the database fixtures create accounts with well-known passwords, including an administrator account 'superadmin' with password 'superadmin' (is_admin=TRUE, line 10) and user accounts with passwords 'password' and 'spidey' (lines 11-13). Anyone with access to this app can log in as the administrator.
